questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Pipe Flow Analysis and Pipe Networks (Hardy Cross Method)
questions.text: Explain Pipe Network Analysis using Hardy Cross Method. Derive flow correction formula $\Delta Q = -\frac{\sum r Q_0 |Q_0|^{n-1}}{n \sum r |Q_0|^{n-1}}$ for a closed loop. Perform one iteration for a given two-loop pipe network.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Pipe Flow Analysis and Pipe Networks (Hardy Cross Method)
questions.text: Explain Water Hammer phenomenon in pipes. Derive acoustic wave velocity $c = \sqrt{\frac{K/\rho}{1 + (K/E)(D/t)}}$. Differentiate between Rapid Closure ($t_c < \frac{2L}{c}$) and Slow Closure ($t_c > \frac{2L}{c}$). Explain Surge Tanks and Air Vessels.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Uniform Flow in Open Channels (Manning's and Chezy's Formula)
questions.text: State Chezy's and Manning's formulas for uniform open channel flow ($v = \frac{1}{n} R^{2/3} S_0^{1/2}$). Derive conditions for Most Economical (Hydraulically Efficient) channel sections for: (a) Rectangular section ($b = 2y, R = y/2$), and (b) Trapezoidal section ($R = y/2$, side slope $\theta = 60^\circ$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Energy and Momentum Principles in Open Channel Flow
questions.text: Define Specific Energy ($E = y + \frac{q^2}{2g y^2}$) in open channels. Draw Specific Energy curve. Derive Critical Depth ($y_c = \left(\frac{q^2}{g}\right)^{1/3}$), Minimum Specific Energy ($E_{min} = \frac{3}{2} y_c$), and condition for Froude Number $Fr = 1$ at critical flow.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Energy and Momentum Principles in Open Channel Flow
questions.text: Explain Channel Transitions: Flow over a broad-crested weir and flow through a channel constriction/width reduction. Explain Choking condition in supercritical and subcritical flows.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Non-Uniform Gradually Varied Flow (GVF) and Water Surface Profiles
questions.text: Derive the Dynamic Equation of Gradually Varied Flow (GVF): $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{S_0 - S_f}{1 - Fr^2}$. Classify and sketch all 12 water surface profiles (Mild: $M_1, M_2, M_3$; Steep: $S_1, S_2, S_3$; Critical: $C_1, C_3$; Horizontal: $H_2, H_3$; Adverse: $A_2, A_3$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Non-Uniform Gradually Varied Flow (GVF) and Water Surface Profiles
questions.text: Explain Direct Step Method and Standard Step Method for computation of GVF surface profile length between two sections.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Rapidly Varied Flow (RVF) and Hydraulic Jump
questions.text: Explain Hydraulic Jump in a horizontal rectangular channel. Derive the Belanger Equation for conjugate depths: $\frac{y_2}{y_1} = \frac{1}{2} \left( \sqrt{1 + 8 Fr_1^2} - 1 \right)$. Derive expression for energy loss in jump $\Delta E = \frac{(y_2 - y_1)^3}{4 y_1 y_2}$ and explain Stilling Basins.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Hydraulic Turbines (Pelton, Francis, Kaplan) and Centrifugal Pumps
questions.text: Explain Hydraulic Turbines: Classify Impulse Turbine (Pelton Wheel) vs Reaction Turbines (Francis, Kaplan). Draw velocity triangles and derive expression for hydraulic efficiency $\eta_h$. Define Specific Speed ($N_s = \frac{N \sqrt{P}}{H^{5/4}}$) and Unit Quantities ($N_u, Q_u, P_u$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Hydraulic Turbines (Pelton, Francis, Kaplan) and Centrifugal Pumps
questions.text: Explain Centrifugal Pumps: Working principle, velocity triangles, Manometric Head ($H_m$), Manometric Efficiency, Cavitation, and Net Positive Suction Head (NPSH).
